text:
jordan: Hey infra team — my GitOps PR (#4827) is blocked by an OPA pre-merge policy. This is a CI-only change (add small GPU test nodepool) but OPA is flagging a cost rule. Can someone quick-review so we don't hold the whole test pipeline. PR: https://git.company/repo/ops/4827

policy-bot: PRE-MERGE CHECK FAILED
- rule: cost/require-approval-for-gpu-pool-upsizes
- msg: Proposed change increases GPU capacity (nv6b) in project 'redwood-ci' by 2 nodes (~$1200/mo). Approval required from "cost-approvers" or an explicit policy exemption.
- details:
```
  # terraform plan snippet
  + module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance_group_manager.gpu[0]
    machine_type: "n1-standard-16" -> "n1-standard-16+nv6b"
    gpu_count: 0 -> 1
    labels: { env = "ci" }
```

jordan: This is just a transient CI job pool used for nightly E2E tests (non-prod). We spin it up for 30m, run tests, then destroy. The cost estimate in the plan is inflated because pricing assumes 24/7. The change is targeted to namespace "ci-nightly" only.

sara: Can you paste the PR diff for the module? I want to confirm it's scoped to the ci project and not touching prod pools.

jordan: Sure — diff below:
```
resource "redwood_gpu_pool" "ci_test_pool" {
  project = "redwood-ci"
  count   = 1
  machine = "nv6b"
  lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
  annotations = { "ci-only" = "true", "ttl-minutes" = "60" }
}
```

mike: If it's annotated with ci-only + ttl, we should be able to get a quick exemption. OPA rule is broad (any nv6b in infra repos), so the path is either: 1) add an explicit policy-exemption label that policy-bot recognizes, or 2) get a manual sign-off from cost-approvers. Option 1 is faster for CI.

julia: Who's on the cost approvers list this week? We had a freeze window starting tomorrow — does that affect manual overrides?

infra-oncall: I'm oncall today. Freeze window is for prod promotions and quotas; ephemeral CI pools are exempt from the freeze if they are in projects with tag "ci-exempt". Is the project tagged?

jordan: project "redwood-ci" has tag: ci-exempt: true (see project metadata). I can also add `policy_exemption = "ephemeral-ci"` annotation to the terraform resource so policy-bot will skip it. Want me to push that?

policy-bot: NOTE: only maintainers with label `policy:allow-ephemeral-ci` can add policy_exemption without manual review. Otherwise the check still fails.

ben: Quick risk assessment — ephemeral CI pools get created/destroyed by pipeline runner, no secrets and no network egress to prod VPCs. I'm okay with a scoped exemption. Jordan: add the annotation and ping me, I'll approve in the policy dashboard (takes 2-3 minutes). Also leave a one-line note in the PR describing cost controls and TTL.

jordan: Adding annotation now and will update PR. Pushing a tiny change in 1m.

jordan: (update) pushed patch: added `annotations = { "policy_exemption" = "ephemeral-ci", "ci-only" = "true" }` and PR description note.

policy-bot: RE-RUNNING CHECKS...
- status: needs-manual-approval
- reason: policy_exemption tag present but requires approval from a policy approver for this repo.

ben: @jordan I approved the exemption in the policy dashboard. Please rebase and re-run the pipeline, I'll watch.

jordan: Rebased and pipeline retriggered. Tests starting. Thanks all :thumbsup: :party_parrot:

sara: Good call adding TTL and note. When this is merged, can we also add a brief runbook snippet to the repo describing the approval path for ephemeral pools? Saves future context.

jordan: Agreed — filing a follow-up PR for runbook after merge.

ben: Marking as resolved from cost side. If anything flares, @infra-oncall please escalate and tag `cost-ops`.

infra-oncall: Noted. Monitoring now.

jordan: Final status: pipeline green, merge queued. Thanks everyone!
